title: Repository instructions
when: Always on. Conventions every request in this repo should follow.
body: Added to chat requests automatically. Keep it to the rules that matter most; every line is sent with every prompt. /init can draft one for you.
example:
# Project rules
- TypeScript strict; no `any`.
- React function components and hooks only.
- Tests live next to the code: foo.ts → foo.test.ts (Vitest).
- Use the logger in src/lib/log.ts, never console.log.

# How to reply
- Keep replies short: what changed and what to check.
- Don't add dependencies without asking.

title: Path-specific instructions
when: Only when matching files are in play, e.g. SQL migrations or tests.
body: The applyTo glob in the front matter decides when the file is used, so specialist rules don’t cost tokens on unrelated work.
example:
---
applyTo: "db/migrations/**/*.sql"
---
- Every migration must be reversible: include a down step.
- Never drop a column in the same release that stops using it.
- Name files YYYYMMDDHHMM_short_description.sql.

title: Prompt files
when: Prompts you run again and again: reviews, release notes, new endpoints.
body: Run one with /name in chat. The front matter can set the agent, model and tools, so a cheap model can handle routine prompts. /create-prompt writes one for you.
example:
---
name: review-diff
description: Review my uncommitted changes
agent: ask
---
Review #changes as a senior engineer.
List at most 8 issues, most serious first: bugs, missing tests, security, naming.
One line each with file:line. No praise, no summary.

title: Custom agents
when: A role with its own rules and tools, like a reviewer that can’t edit.
body: Formerly called custom chat modes. Pick one from the Agent dropdown. Limiting tools keeps it safe and keeps tool output out of the context.
example:
---
description: Read-only reviewer for pull requests
tools: ['search', 'read']
---
You review code. Never edit files.
Check: correctness, tests, security, naming, dead code.
Reply as a numbered list, most serious first, max 10 items.

title: AGENTS.md
when: Repos shared with other AI tools that also read AGENTS.md.
body: A root AGENTS.md is used as context by default (chat.useAgentsMdFile). Use it instead of copilot-instructions.md if your team uses several AI tools. Don’t keep both saying the same thing.
example:
# AGENTS.md
## Build and test
- npm ci && npm test
- npm run lint must pass before commit.

## Conventions
- API handlers in src/api/<resource>.ts, one per resource.
- Errors: throw AppError from src/lib/errors.ts.

title: Agent skills
when: A repeatable procedure with steps and supporting files, like a release checklist.
body: Skills are folders with a SKILL.md and any scripts or templates it needs. Run one with /<name>.
example:
---
name: release-notes
description: Draft release notes from merged PRs
---
1. List PRs merged since the last tag.
2. Group them: Features, Fixes, Internal.
3. One line per PR, user-facing wording, link the PR.
